pull.title: cli: respect -rpcclienttimeout even when sending
pull.body:
The move away from libevent introduced a small regression in this regard. In #36299, we switched the timeout to apply per socket wait, but continued on to another socket wait in case of timeout, instead of returning. See commit message for details.

In general, we also shouldn't ignore `Sock::Wait`'s errors and timeouts by silently retrying forever.

Fix these issues by returning instead when `Sock::Wait` times out or returns an error. ~~Tentative bot functional test for this in second commit that appears to be robust enough.~~

events.message:
cli: fail to send a request when the socket does not become writable

HTTPClient::SendRequest() waits for the socket to become writable and
went back to waiting whenever Sock::Wait() returned without SendEvent.
Before 1805716354, the `continue` was the route to the deadline check. That
commit removed the deadline, so a Sock::Wait() timeout silently started
waiting again, forever. This means -rpcclienttimeout is never respected
when sending: bitcoin-cli will hang for as long as the server keeps the
connection open without reading the request.

Fix this by returning a failure whenever `Sock::Wait()` timeouts or errors.

Well, scratch that. It's flaky on Windows. I'm dropping it from this PR: reviewers can easily bot-implement one locally to sanity check the behaviour. The only robust alternative would be a unit test, but would require some refactoring. That's overkill for this PR's trivial fix to the CLI.

tested ACK e5d9a7e04b50c723aeb65984e5048ffd098f6737

I also had it in my backlog (came up a few weeks ago when I was reviewing a different change - cc: @maflcko).
Tested locally that a stalled upload reports a send failure and that the provided fix is correct.

ACK e5d9a7e04b50c723aeb65984e5048ffd098f6737

Built and tested on macos/arm64.

The undesired behavior is not just an ordinary timeout while waiting for a server reply, but a timeout while waiting for the socket to be writable on the client end. Even if no server exists at all, the client's kernel's TCP stack may still happily receive bytes with no where to send them.

To reproduce I ran a trivial accept-and-do-not-read server and made bitcoin-cli connections to it. The only way to garuntee the "wait forever" behavior is to send an excessive amount of data with bitcoin-cli and trigger TCP backpressure so the socket actually becomes not writable.

On master, in that case, we `continue` to wait forever. With this patch, we quit with `(Failed to send HTTP request)`.

One thing thats not exactly clear in the PR description or commit message is that a timeout is NOT treated as an error. `select()` and `poll()` return `0` on timeout, and so `Wait()` and `WaitMany()` still return `true`. On master, we already quit on error. This PR also quits on timeout.
